newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium bans air shows pending crash report.
newsitem.headline: Belgium bans air shows pending crash report.

text.p: Belgium has banned all air shows on military airfields pending a report into safety at such events after nine people died in a crash last week.

Defence Minister Jean-Paul Poncelet ordered the armed forces and judicial authorities to investigate problems posed by air shows including security and disaster liability, his deputy chief of staff Ludwig Van der Veken told Belga news agency on Saturday.

In last Saturday's disaster, a plane piloted by the leader of the Jordanian air force display team spun out of control and smashed into a crowd of people around a Red Cross tent during an air display at Ostend airport on the Belgian coast.

Belga quoted Van der Veken as saying no air shows would be authorised at military facilities while the investigation was under way. The first to be cancelled would be a show scheduled for August 23 and 24 at an airbase near the western town of Kortrijk.
"This inquiry will most likely take several weeks," Van der Veken was quoted as saying.
Air shows regularly attract tens of thousands of people during the summer in Belgium.

Since last week's disaster there have been numerous calls for shows at civilian airports to be banned in Belgium, which has stringent safety rules. A preliminary report into the causes of the crash is due on August 15.
A memorial service was held on Saturday for the victims of the crash.
Jordan's Queen Noor was in Belgium on Thursday and Friday to pay condolences to the families of the victims.
